sections.html:
Huntley is a village in the northwest Chicago area that straddles McHenry County and Kane County. It lies along Interstate 90 and uses ZIP code 60142. Three townships divide it. Land north of Kreutzer Road is in Grafton Township, and land south of Kreutzer Road is in Rutland Township, except the northwest end of Sun City, which is in Hampshire Township. The county and township decide which office handles your tax bill and your deed.

Growth has been fast. The count was 5,730 in 2000, 24,291 in 2010 and 27,740 in 2020, and the mid-2025 estimate is 29,132.

For 2020 to 2024, 88.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the median value is $334,300, and there are 12,213 households. A large share of residents are 65 or older, which often means estate sales, downsizing and moves to be near family. Because so many homes are owned, most sales are owner-to-owner rather than investor deals. Sun City, the age-restricted community reached by Del Webb Boulevard, is its own submarket and has its own garbage arrangement.

Illinois Route 47 is the main north-south road and runs nearly seven miles through the village. It was widened from two to five lanes in 2011, carries over 20,000 vehicles a day, and meets I-90 at a full interchange finished in November 2013. Algonquin Road runs east toward Algonquin and Lake in the Hills, and Main Street connects west toward Marengo and Harmony Road. Huntley-Dundee Road leads east to the Carpentersville and Dundee area.

Mean commute is 29.5 minutes. A listing can point to the I-90 and Route 47 access as a practical selling point.

Huntley Community School District 158 serves the village. Huntley High School is on Harmony Road, and the middle schools are Marlowe in Lake in the Hills and Heineman in Algonquin.

  • The Huntley Fire Protection District covers about 55 square miles and serves all village residents.
  • The Huntley Area Public Library is on Ruth Road. The Hampshire Township part of the village is served by the Ella Johnson Memorial Public Library.
  • The Huntley Park District runs the recreation center on Mill Street.
  • Residential garbage goes through a single village-wide hauler with Monday pickup, except apartments and Sun City.

Huntley does not charge a real estate transfer stamp, and it does not require village stickers. That removes one trip to Village Hall.

State law still applies. Illinois taxes the transfer of title itself under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, and a mortgage the buyer takes over can be left out of the taxable value if the deed says so. Ask the title company which county charges apply to a McHenry County parcel and which to a Kane County parcel.

Most home improvements in the village need a permit, and Development Services at 847-515-5252 can confirm whether a past project was permitted. If you finished a basement, deck or similar work, find the permit paperwork before you list.

Call the office that matches where the parcel sits.

Where the parcel sitsOffice to call

The back of your tax bill shows the taxing districts that levy against the house, and the closing attorney can use it to prorate the bill at closing.

Buyers often ask about local rules before they make an offer.

  • Watering follows a four-tier color-coded conservation program (red, yellow, orange and green), with signs posted around the village.
  • The village applies the McHenry County Open Burning Ordinance to all property inside its limits, and because lots are small, leaf burning is essentially illegal for most homeowners.
  • There is no village pet license, but McHenry and Kane counties both require rabies tags for dogs.
  • A garage sale needs no permit, though signs may go only on private property.
  • Recreational vehicle parking and storage fall under Zoning Code Section 156.106.
  • Overnight parking on village streets is prohibited from 2 a.m. to 6 a.m.
  • Yard waste is collected from April 1 to November 30, and the village runs a branch pick-up program twice a year.

Handing a buyer this short list in advance saves questions during negotiations.

sections.h2: How can you sell a Huntley house quickly?
sections.html:
Three routes are open, and the right one depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close.

  • Hire an agent and list. This tends to reach the most buyers and suits a house in good shape.
  • Sell it yourself. You keep the whole process in your hands, including the contract and the disclosures.
  • Take a cash offer. It can work for an inherited house, a rental, or a place that needs repairs you do not want to fund, and the closing date can be set around your plans.

Before choosing, confirm the county for the parcel, collect any permit records, and ask the water billing office about a final reading. With no village stamp to buy, Huntley sales can move on a short schedule once the contract is signed.

A cash buyer does not need a mortgage, so the sale does not wait on a lender's appraisal or a loan approval. That matters most for the sellers Huntley has plenty of: people settling an estate, moving closer to family, or leaving a rental they no longer want to manage.

The house is taken as it stands, so you can skip repair work and a round of showings. You still owe the same state transfer tax and the same prorated tax bill, and you still need to know your county. Ask for the closing date in writing, and ask who covers each closing charge before you sign. If the buyer will pay the title company fees, confirm that in the contract too, and keep a copy of the final settlement statement once the sale is done.

sections.h2: Steps from signed contract to keys
sections.html:
The sequence is short in Huntley because the village adds no stamp. Still, a few items need to be lined up.

  1. Confirm which county and township your parcel is in, using the Kreutzer Road split described above.
  2. Gather permit records for any basement, deck or similar work and give them to the buyer or title company.
  3. Ask the water billing office for a final reading.
  4. Have the title company work out the state transfer tax and the county charges for your county.
  5. Prorate the tax bill at closing, using the taxing districts printed on the back of your bill.

Sellers who are in Sun City should also tell the buyer about the separate garbage arrangement, since it differs from the village-wide hauler.

faqs.q: What is the population of Huntley, IL?
faqs.a: The mid-2025 estimate is 29,132. The 2020 census counted 27,740.

faqs.q: Does Huntley require a real estate transfer stamp?
faqs.a: No. The village requires neither a transfer stamp nor village stickers. Illinois state transfer tax still applies.
McHenry County and Kane County. Land north of Kreutzer Road is in Grafton Township, and most land south of it is in Rutland Township.
Huntley Community School District 158 serves the village, with Huntley High School on Harmony Road.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property taxes on a Huntley house?
faqs.a: Call the McHenry County Assessor's Office at 815-334-4290 or Kane County at 630-232-5950, depending on where the parcel lies. The township numbers are in the table above.
